Rashi on Nedarim 7b:2:1.hebrew: קסבר במשמתנא פליגי - דהכא משמתנא קאמר, וקאמר ליה רב חסדא לית דחש לה להא דר"ע, דהוה אוסר במנודה אני לך, דהיינו משמתנא:
Rashi on Nedarim 7b:2:1.english: [Rav Ḥisda] holds [that] they disagree regarding "I am excommunicated" - For here [the man] said "I am excommunicated," and Rav Ḥisda said to him, "There is no one who is concerned for that [opinion] of Rabbi Akiva," who would prohibit [a vow made with] "I am ostracized from you," which is [equivalent to] "I am excommunicated."

Rashi on Nedarim 7b:3:1.hebrew: נידהו בפניו - חכם שנידה את האדם בפניו, אין יכול להתיר לו אלא בפניו:
Rashi on Nedarim 7b:3:1.english: [If] one ostracized him in his presence - A sage who ostracized a person in his presence cannot dissolve [it] for him except in his presence.

Rashi on Nedarim 7b:4:1.english: Mention of the Name - That he utters the Name of Heaven in vain.

Rashi on Nedarim 7b:5:1.english: As it is stated: “For all the men are dead” - And we say: these are Dathan and Abiram, who fell into poverty.

Rashi on Nedarim 7b:5:2.hebrew: כל מקום שנתנו חכמים עיניהם - לאדם שנידו, או מת או נופל בעניות; ואהכי צריך לנדותו כדי שיפול בעניות, דהיינו כמיתה:
Rashi on Nedarim 7b:5:2.english: Wherever the Sages set their eyes - [That is,] upon a person whom they excommunicated, either he dies or he falls into poverty; and therefore one must excommunicate him, so that he will fall into poverty, which is like death.

Rashi on Nedarim 7b:6:1.hebrew: אין בין נידוי להפרה ולא כלום - דלא צריך להיות יום או יומים בנידוי, דהא לאלתר שרא לה:
Rashi on Nedarim 7b:6:1.english: There is nothing between ostracism and nullification - For [one] does not need to be in ostracism for a day or two, since [Rav Huna] immediately dissolved [it] for her.

Rashi on Nedarim 7b:8:1.english: What are the circumstances - That he excommunicates himself.

Rashi on Nedarim 7b:8:2.english: And he enters his home and dissolves [it] for him - For he did not excommunicate him in his presence.

Tosafot on Nedarim 7b:1:1.hebrew: במאי פליגי במנודה אני לך דר"ע סבר לישנא דנדינא הוא - שיהא נע ונד ומרוחק מהנאתו, דאין לספקו בלשון נידוי ולענין הרחקת ד' אמות. אף על גב דלשון המשנה קורא "מנודה" שנדוהו, כדאמרי' מ"ק (דף טו:): "מנודה לא שונה ולא שונין לו", מכל מקום כשאדם רוצה להרחיק עצמו ד' אמות, אינו רגיל להזכיר נידוי על עצמו בשביל כך. הלכך על כרחך לישנא דנדינא הוא כדפי', ושפיר הוי ידים מוכיחות בלא "שאני אוכל לך":
Tosafot on Nedarim 7b:1:1.english: What do they disagree about? [With regard to] "I am ostracized (menuddeh) from you," as Rabbi Akiva holds it is a language of nedina (distancing) - [Meaning] that he should be a wanderer (na va-nad) and distanced from deriving benefit from him, for one should not treat it as doubtful [that he meant it] as an expression of excommunication (niddui) and with regard to distancing four cubits. Even though Mishnaic usage calls one whom they excommunicated "menuddeh," as we say in Moed Katan (15b): "An excommunicated person neither teaches nor do [others] teach him," nevertheless, when a person wishes to distance himself four cubits [from someone], he is not accustomed to invoke excommunication upon himself for that purpose. Therefore, perforce it is a language of nedina, as I explained, and it is indeed a clear intimation (yadayim mochichot) [of a vow] even without [adding] "that I will eat of yours."

Tosafot on Nedarim 7b:3:1.hebrew: נדהו בפניו אין מתירין לו אלא בפניו - יש לפרש דשפיר מועיל גם שלא בפניו, אלא לכבודו של מנודה, דכמו שביישו לפניו כך יש לפייסו לפניו, אע"פ שנדהו בדין. אי נמי, בעי למימר דכיון שנדוהו בפניו, אלים הנידוי כל כך שלא יועיל ההיתר אלא בפניו, כעין שנדהו. ודכוותה אמרינן בגיטין (דף לג:): "כל מילתא דמתאמרא בפני י' צריכא בי י' [למשלפא]":
Tosafot on Nedarim 7b:3:1.english: If one ostracized him in his presence, one may dissolve it for him only in his presence - One may explain that [dissolving it] is indeed effective even not in his presence, rather [this requirement is] for the honor of the ostracized person: for just as he shamed him in his presence, so must he appease him in his presence, even though he ostracized him lawfully. Alternatively, [the Gemara] means to say that since they ostracized him in his presence, the ostracism is so potent that the dissolution is not effective except in his presence, similar to [the manner in which] they ostracized him. And similarly we say in Gittin (33b): "Any matter that is stated in the presence of ten requires ten [to undo it]."

Tosafot on Nedarim 7b:4:1.english: If he did not ostracize him, he himself shall be ostracized - That is to say, the Sages of the generation are obligated to ostracize him.

Tosafot on Nedarim 7b:4:2.hebrew: שכ"מ שהזכרת השם מצויה עניות מצויה - פי' הרב אלעזר דנפקא לן מדכתיב (שמות כ׳:כ״א): "בכל מקום אשר אזכיר את שמי אבא אליך וברכתיך" — מדהזכרת שם דמצוה גורם ברכה, דהיינו עושר, א"כ הזכרת שם דלבטלה גורם עניות. ור"י פי' דנפקא לן מדכתיב גבי שבועת שקר (זכריה ה׳:ד׳): "ובא אל בית הגנב וכלתו ואת עציו ואבניו", והזכרת השם לבטלה דומה קצת לשבועת שקר:
Tosafot on Nedarim 7b:4:2.english: Wherever mention of [God's] name is common, poverty is common - Rabbi Elazar explained that we derive it from what is written (Exodus 20:21): "In every place where I cause My name to be mentioned, I will come to you and bless you" — since mentioning [God's] name for a mitzvah causes blessing, which is wealth, therefore mentioning [God's] name in vain causes poverty. And Ri explained that we derive it from what is written regarding a false oath (Zechariah 5:4): "And it shall enter the house of the thief [...] and it shall consume it, with its timber and its stones," and mentioning [God's] name in vain is somewhat similar to a false oath.

Tosafot on Nedarim 7b:5:1.hebrew: עניות כמיתה דכתיב כי מתו כל האנשים המבקשים את נפשך - גבי דתן ואבירם, דע"כ לא מתו אז במצרים, שהרי היו במדבר. וליכא למימר שהיו סומין ומצורעים החשובים כמתים: סומין ליכא למימר, דכתיב (במדבר ט״ז:י״ד) "העיני האנשים ההם תנקר"; ומצורעים נמי לא, שהרי היו בקרב ישראל, וליכא למימר שנתרפאו במתן תורה, שהרי חזרו למומן במעשה העגל. וליכא למימר שלא היו להם בנים, דהא כתיב (שם) (הם) "ונשיהם ובניהם וטפם"; ועוד, דמשום שלא היו להם בנים לא נמנעו מלהיות קרובים למלכות כבתחילה, אבל בשביל עניות ודאי נמנעו מלהיות קרובים למלכות:
Tosafot on Nedarim 7b:5:1.english: Poverty is like death, as it is written: "For all the men who sought your life are dead" - [This refers to] Dathan and Abiram, for perforce they did not die then in Egypt, since they were in the wilderness. And one cannot say that they were blind or lepers, who are considered like the dead: one cannot say [they were] blind, as it is written (Numbers 16:14): "Will you put out the eyes of those men?"; and [they were] not lepers either, since they were among Israel, and one cannot say that they were healed at the giving of the Torah, since they reverted to their blemishes at the incident of the Golden Calf. And one cannot say that they had no children, for it is written (ibid.): "(They,) and their wives, and their sons, and their little ones"; and furthermore, because of not having children they would not have been prevented from being close to royalty as before, whereas because of poverty they were certainly prevented from being close to royalty.

Tosafot on Nedarim 7b:6:1.hebrew: אין בין נידוי להפרה ולא כלום - תימה, דאמרי' במ"ק (דף טז.): "טוט אסר וטוט שרי", פי': לאלתר; ה"מ לענין מנודה, אבל לענין אפקירותא — עד דחייל עליה שמתא תלתין יומין. וי"ל: ה"נ, כיון שנידוי זה אינו אלא לכפרה בעלמא וחיישי' עליו שלא ירגיל עוד להזכיר שם שמים לבטלה, אין זה נידוי חשוב כאפקירותא לשאר עבירות לחול עליו נידוי שעה אחת:
Tosafot on Nedarim 7b:6:1.english: There is nothing between ostracism and nullification - It is astonishing, for we say in Mo'ed Katan (16a): "Tut binds and tut releases" [i.e., a shofar blast binds and releases], meaning immediately; [and the Gemara explains there:] this applies only with respect to [an ordinary] ostracized person, but with respect to insolence, [he is not released] until the ostracism has taken effect upon him for thirty days. And one can answer: Here too, since this ostracism is only for mere atonement, and we are concerned about him lest he habituate himself further to mention the Name of Heaven in vain, this is not considered an ostracism like [that for] insolence regarding other transgressions, such that ostracism should take effect upon him [even] for a single hour.

Tosafot on Nedarim 7b:8:1.hebrew: משמת נפשיה והדר משמת בר בי רב - פר"ת שזה היה עושה כדי שלא ישכח להתיר הנידוי של בר בי רב; אבל עכשיו שמשמת נפשיה, מתוך כך שהיה זכור להתיר שלו, זכור יהיה נמי להתיר של בר בי רב. ור"י פירש דלכפרה היה עושה כך, שלא יענש במה שמנדה צורבא מדרבנן, כי בקושי יש לנדותו, כדאמרינן (בפסחים נב.): "ממנו אנגידא ולא ממנו אשמתא". ואע"פ שזה היה מתחייב שמתא מן הדין, אעפ"כ היה ירא מן העונש; לכך היה משמת נפשיה לכפרה:
Tosafot on Nedarim 7b:8:1.english: He excommunicates himself and then excommunicates the student - Rabbeinu Tam explained that he would do this so that he would not forget to release the excommunication of the student; rather, now that he excommunicates himself, since he would remember to release his own [excommunication], he will also remember to release that of the student. And Ri explained that he would do so for atonement, so that he would not be punished for excommunicating a Torah scholar — for one should only excommunicate him with great reluctance, as we say (in Pesachim 52a): "They vote for lashes, and they do not vote for excommunication." And even though this [student] was liable to excommunication according to the law, nevertheless he feared the punishment; therefore, he would excommunicate himself for atonement.

Tosafot on Nedarim 7b:8:2.hebrew: משמת נפשיה - היה מרחיק עצמו ד"א מחביריו:
Tosafot on Nedarim 7b:8:2.english: He would excommunicate himself - He would distance himself four cubits from his colleagues.

Tosafot on Nedarim 7b:8:3.hebrew: כי עייל לביתיה שרי לנפשיה - משום בני ביתיה. והדר שרי לבר בי רב — כדי שיבא זכאי ויכפר על החייב; לכך היה מתיר לעצמו קודם:
Tosafot on Nedarim 7b:8:3.english: When he would enter his home, he would dissolve [the excommunication] for himself - because of the members of his household. And then he would dissolve [it] for the student — so that the innocent one might come and atone for the guilty one; therefore, he would release himself first:
